title: Proper fibre idempotent image over a locally Noetherian base
statement: Let f:X→S be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], S locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and s∈S. For each idempotent e in Γ(X_s,O) on its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], there is an open neighbourhood U of s and t∈Γ(f⁻¹U,O_X) whose pullback along X_s→X is e.

proof.text: (Noetherian case, setup.) In Steps 1-4 assume moreover that $S$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_s$, $M=(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s$ (an $A$-module) and, for $n\ge1$, $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^n$, $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}A_n\times_SX$, so that $X_1=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\times_SX$ is the fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] (up to the symmetry of the fibre product). By the definition of locally Noetherian, $s$ lies in an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq S$ with $B$ Noetherian; $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$ for the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $s$, so $A$ is a Noetherian local ring [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, second paragraph ('Assume S is Noetherian'), lines 8128-8132

proof.text: (Lifting $e$ to the infinitesimal neighbourhoods.) For $n\ge1$, $X_1=X_n\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_n}\operatorname{Spec}(A_n/\mathfrak mA_n)$ (associativity of fibre products, $A_n/\mathfrak mA_n=\kappa(s)$), and the ideal $J=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^n$ of $A_n$ satisfies $J^n=0$. Hence the restriction $\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})\to\Gamma(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})$ along the closed immersion $X_1\to X_n$ is a bijection on idempotents [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-nilpotent-thickening-idempotents] (this is the statement that $X_n$ and $X_s$ have the same underlying space, so the decomposition $X_s=T_1\amalg T_2$ given by $e$ lifts to $X_n$). Let $e_n\in\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ be the unique idempotent restricting to $e$. For $n\le n'$ the restriction of $e_{n'}$ to $X_n$ is an idempotent whose restriction to $X_1$ is $e$ (the composite $X_1\to X_n\to X_{n'}$ is the closed immersion $X_1\to X_{n'}$), so it equals $e_n$ by uniqueness. Thus $(e_n)_n\in\varprojlim_n H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, with first component $e_1=e$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8133-8146 ('Since the underlying topological space of X_n is equal to that of X_s ... e_{n+1} restricts to e_n on X_n')

proof.text: (Formal functions.) By the theorem on formal functions at $s$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-functions-stalk] with $p=0$ and $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ ($f$ proper, $S$ locally Noetherian, $\mathcal O_X$ coherent), the maps $\theta_n:M\to H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ (pull back a germ of a section of $\mathcal O_X$ over $f^{-1}(V)$ to $X_n$) induce an $A$-linear isomorphism $\theta:M^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, $M^\wedge=\varprojlim_nM/\mathfrak m^nM$, with $\theta\circ\iota=(\theta_n)_n$ for the canonical map $\iota:M\to M^\wedge$. Note that $\theta_1:M\to H^0(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})=H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ is the map of the statement. Put $e_\infty=\theta^{-1}((e_n)_n)\in M^\wedge$; its image under the first component of $\theta$ is $e$.

source.place: proof of Lemma 0G7X, lines 8132-8149, citing Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02OD (coherent-lemma-formal-functions-stalk)

proof.text: (Descending from the completion.) Since $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated, the projection $p_1:M^\wedge\to M/\mathfrak mM$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak mM^\wedge$, and $p_1\circ\iota$ is the quotient map $M\to M/\mathfrak mM$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] (part (2), $n=1$; this is Algebra 05GG, $M^\wedge/\mathfrak mM^\wedge=M/\mathfrak mM$). Choose $x\in M$ with $p_1(\iota(x))=p_1(e_\infty)$; then $\iota(x)-e_\infty\in\mathfrak mM^\wedge$, so, $\theta$ being $A$-linear, $\theta(\iota(x))-(e_n)_n\in\mathfrak m\cdot\varprojlim_nH^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$. Its first component lies in $\mathfrak m\,H^0(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})=0$, since $A$ acts on $H^0(X_1,\mathcal O_{X_1})$ through $A\to\kappa(s)$ ($X_1$ is a scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$). Hence $\theta_1(x)=e_1=e$, i.e. $e$ is in the image of $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_s\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$. This proves the lemma when $S$ is locally Noetherian.
